title: Language Modelling
blurb: How a language model is actually built, from raw bytes to a system that follows instructions — BPE and the cross-entropy objective, attention derived from scratch, the 6ND rule and Chinchilla allocation (including the published fit that does not reproduce its own paper's recommendation), MoE, GQA/MLA, DPO and GRPO. Follows the arc of Stanford CS336; every paper checked against arXiv.

title: Bayesian Optimization
blurb: How to find the best settings of an expensive black-box function in a few dozen tries — Gaussian process surrogates and acquisition functions derived by hand, a live GP playground, and the 2024–26 fights over high dimensions and LLMs. Every paper arXiv-verified.

title: Diffusion Language Models
blurb: Why frontier LLMs type one token at a time, and how diffusion lets them paint the whole answer instead — from Gaussian noise to masked tokens to Mercury, grounded in the nine papers on Inception Labs' about page.
